correctness.rationale: Strict-poset finite-extension criteria are established by transitive closure, confirmed on 2367 small diagrams. Each pair gives four cuts per old chain; weak-order strata are products of binomial-polynomial counts of degree <=4 per chain. A positive 5x5 interpolation grid and separate positive axes prove the explicit polynomial formulas for all nonnegative lengths. All calculations are reproduced by verify.py and its saved output.

value.rationale: Disjoint unions of two chains form the exact equality family of an established unary extension-type bound; classifying their two-point spectrum is a natural next invariant. The non-obvious exact law I=N(2N+1)/3, uniform comparable fraction >1/2 and its unbalanced half-limit are structural properties not read off unary counts. The factorisation fails outside this family (e.g. a fork base), delimiting a motivated boundary.
